test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 7 Oct 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: An electric lamp of 40 Ω, a toaster of resistance 200 Ω and a water filter of resistance 400 Ω are connected in parallel to a 220 V source. Suppose an electric iron when connected to a 220 V source draws the same current as that of the three appliances in the above, then the resistance and current flowing through the iron are:
solution:
The correct answer is __**30.77 Ω and 7.15 A, respectively**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Given an electric lamp, a toaster, and a water filter with resistances of 40 Ω, 200 Ω, and 400 Ω respectively are connected in parallel.
 
• The equivalent resistance (Rₑq) of these resistors in parallel is calculated using the formula:

 1/Rₑq = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + 1/R₃.
 
• **Applying the formula**: 1/Rₑq = 1/40 + 1/200 + 1/400 = (10+2.5+1.25)/400 = 13.75/400, Rₑq = 400/13.75 ≈ 29.09 Ω.
 
• The total current (I) drawn from the source is I = V/Rₑq = 220 V / 29.09 Ω ≈ 7.57 A.
 
• An electric iron drawing the same current (7.57 A) from a 220 V source has a resistance R = V/I = 220 V / 7.57 A ≈ 29.07 Ω, which matches closely with option 4.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm's Law**

 
 
• Ohm's Law states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
 
• The formula is V = IR, where V is voltage, I is current, and R is resistance.
 
 
 
• **Parallel Circuit**
 
 
• In a parallel circuit, the voltage across each component is the same, while the total current is the sum of the currents through each component.
 
• The reciprocal of the total resistance is the sum of the reciprocals of the individual resistances.
 
 
 
• **Power Consumption**
 
 
• Power consumed by an electrical device is given by P = VI, where P is power, V is voltage, and I is current.
 
• In a resistive circuit, power can also be calculated using P = I²R or P = V²/R.
 
 
 
• **Resistance and Conductance**
 
 
• Resistance is a measure of the opposition to the flow of current in a conductor, while conductance is the measure of the ease with which current flows.
 
• Conductance is the reciprocal of resistance, G = 1/R, and is measured in Siemens (S).
